s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive painful swelling and infiltration of the face, hands, and other areas with a rapid decline in functional status
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the face, particularly affecting the eyelids, periorbital tissues, and hands
Striking infiltration of the eyelids and periorbital skin with multiple firm tumorous swellings
Diffusely rippled appearance of the skin on the forehead, neck, shoulders, and anterior chest
Swollen hands and fingers with scattered focal purpuric infarcts
key_facts: Increasing drowsiness and weakness over 7 days
Dermal oedema and scattered histiocytes on biopsy
Widespread fibrinoid exudates within deeper tissues
Granulomatous inflammation with intense neutrophilic abscesses in subcutaneous fat
Mucin stains (PAS, Alcian blue) initially negative
Hale's colloidal iron staining showed deep dermal mucin

shortlist.label: Scleromyxedema
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of progressive painful swelling, infiltration of the skin, and mucin deposition on biopsy

shortlist.label: Erythema nodosum
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of painful swelling and presence of granulomatous inflammation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Swollen hands and fingers with scattered focal purpuric infarcts and granulomatous inflammation on biopsy

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of granulomatous inflammation and neutrophilic abscesses on biopsy, although no eosinophilia

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Granulomatous inflammation on biopsy and systemic symptoms such as progressive weakness

raw.rationale: The presence of mucin in the skin, as shown by Hale's colloidal iron staining, along with dermal oedema, scattered histiocytes, and granulomatous inflammation, are characteristic features of scleromyxedema. The clinical presentation of progressive painful swelling, particularly affecting the eyelids, periorbital tissues, and hands, also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erythema nodosum
rejected.why: Erythema nodosum typically presents with tender, erythematous nodules on the lower extremities, which does not match the patient's presentation of widespread swelling and mucin deposition.

rejected.label: Panniculitis
rejected.why: While panniculitis can cause swelling and inflammation of subcutaneous fat, the presence of mucin and the specific pattern of granulomatous inflammation in this case are more suggestive of scleromyxedema.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis typically involves the respiratory tract and kidneys, and is associated with a different set of laboratory and pathological findings, such as eosinophilia and anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Sarcoidosis can cause granulomatous inflammation, but it typically involves the lungs and lymph nodes, and is not associated with the same degree of mucin deposition and dermal oedema seen in this case.
